name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Sixteen thousand acres of tidal salt marsh and impoundments on the Delaware Bay where hundreds of thousands of shorebirds stop in May and eagles nest within sight of the road.
buzz: The auto tour loop is the way in and the observation tower at Raymond Pool is where the photographers set up; bring bug spray in summer.

name: Air Mobility Command Museum
unique: A hangar of C-5s, C-141s and a C-47 restored as a D-Day aircraft, plus the only B-17 in Delaware, free and walk around open.
buzz: Volunteers are often retired loadmasters and will open cockpits; the C-5 is the size people cannot get over.

name: Dover Motor Speedway
unique: A mile concrete oval known as the Monster Mile, with banking that lets you see the whole field from the frontstretch and a campground that becomes a small city.
buzz: Fans say the concrete makes the racing better and the traffic easier than the big tracks; the September race is the traditional weekend.

name: Hagley Museum
unique: The du Pont gunpowder works on the Brandywine, with water powered mills you walk through, a powder yard demonstration that shakes the valley and the family mansion.
buzz: The explosion demonstration is the reason children agree to the museum; the walk along the raceway is beautiful and mostly shaded.

name: Delaware Art Museum
unique: The largest collection of Pre-Raphaelite art in the country outside Britain, in a bank building on a wooded park, with a strong Howard Pyle illustration collection.
buzz: The Pre-Raphaelites are the surprise and the American illustration galleries the local pride; it is a two hour museum and free on Sundays.

name: Bethany Beach Boardwalk
unique: A quiet half mile boardwalk with a bandstand, a totem pole and a beach that is calmer than Rehoboth's, in a town that bans alcohol on the sand.
buzz: Families choose it for the calm water and the quiet; the boardwalk is a walk, not a carnival, and parking is free but tight.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park
unique: A barrier beach between the ocean and Rehoboth Bay, with a surfing beach on the inlet side, a fishing pier and a campground under the bridge.
buzz: The inlet is where the surf is consistent and the bay side is flat for kayaks; the bridge traffic in summer is the local joke.

name: Great Falls Tavern
unique: The Potomac pouring over a quarter mile of rock ledges at the fall line, with a 1831 tavern, a canal boat, a mule drawn ride and a cliff trail above the gorge.
buzz: The Billy Goat Trail is the real hike and the section A scramble is the local test; go early, the lot fills by nine on weekends.

name: Glen Echo Park
unique: A 1891 trolley park and Chautauqua that became an arts center, with a 1921 carousel, a Spanish ballroom with swing dances and a glass studio.
buzz: The Saturday night swing dance in the ballroom is the local institution; the art studios are open to walk through and the carousel is two dollars.

name: US Naval Academy
unique: The yard where every American naval officer is trained, with a chapel crypt holding John Paul Jones, a 1906 chapel dome and a museum of ship models.
buzz: The guided tour is free and walks you past the midshipmen, who are still in formation; visitors need a government ID and the museum is separate.

name: Sandy Point State Park
unique: A bay beach under the Chesapeake Bay Bridge with calm water, a fishing pier and a view of the bridge towers from the sand.
buzz: The beach is the easy swim for children and the bridge view at sunset is the photograph; the lot fills early on summer weekends.

name: B&O Ellicott City Station
unique: The oldest railroad station in the country, built 1831 on the B&O's first line, with a turntable, a freight house and a model of the Patapsco valley line.
buzz: The building and the turntable are the reason to come; the town around it floods in heavy rain and the hill is steep.

name: Merriweather Post Pavilion
unique: A pavilion in the woods of Symphony Woods where the lawn slopes into the trees and the summer lineup runs from the symphony to indie rock.
buzz: The lawn is the reason people go and the sound is better than most amphitheaters; parking is a walk and the shows run late.

name: Catoctin Mountain Park
unique: A wooded mountain park built around a CCC camp, with trails to a waterfall and a vista, and Camp David hidden in the next hollow.
buzz: The Cunningham Falls and the Blue Blazes trail are the walks; the park is quiet on weekdays and the presidential retreat is off limits.

name: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
company: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
unique: The story of battlefield medicine in a downtown Frederick building, from amputation tables to the letterman stretcher and the sanitary commission, with a second site at Antietam.
buzz: Nurses and doctors find it fascinating and children find it grim; the guides do not sanitize the surgery.

name: Elk Neck State Park
unique: A peninsula between the Elk and Susquehanna rivers with a bay beach, bluffs, a lighthouse and a campground in the woods.
buzz: The Turkey Point lighthouse trail is the walk and the beach is calm for children; the park is a halfway stop between Baltimore and Philadelphia.

name: Chesapeake City
unique: A canal town split by the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal, with a high bridge over the cut, a waterfront of 19th century houses and ships passing at eye level.
buzz: People stop to watch the ships from the bridge and stay for lunch; the town is small, the canal museum is free and the walk is flat.

name: Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum
unique: A waterfront campus of skipjacks, a lighthouse moved from the bay, a working boatyard and the Hooper Strait screw pile light, with crabbing demonstrations.
buzz: The lighthouse and the skipjack are the highlights and the boatyard is where the work happens; children like the tonging and crab picking.

name: Oxford Bellevue Ferry
unique: The oldest privately operated ferry in the country, a small boat that carries cars and bicycles across the Tred Avon between two colonial towns.
buzz: The crossing is ten minutes and the point is the ride; cyclists use it to loop the Talbot county back roads.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Thirty thousand acres of marsh and open water where the largest breeding population of bald eagles on the east coast nests and thousands of Canada geese winter.
buzz: The wildlife drive at dawn is the experience and the eagle nest is visible from the road; bring bug spray and a scope.

name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Visitor Center
company: National Park Service and Maryland State Parks
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: A visitor center in the marsh landscape Tubman grew up in, telling her story through the places she worked and fled, with a driving tour to the sites.
buzz: The building and the landscape carry the story and rangers lead walks; the driving tour takes a half day and the roads are flat and empty.

name: Calvert Cliffs State Park
unique: A mile and a half walk through woods to a beach below 30 million year old cliffs where shark teeth and shells wash out of the sand.
buzz: Children find teeth within minutes and the walk back is uphill; collecting is allowed from the beach but not the cliffs.

name: Calvert Marine Museum
unique: A museum with river otters, a fossil hall of Miocene whales and a lighthouse, plus a boatyard where a skipjack is restored.
buzz: The otters are the family draw and the fossil hall is serious; the drum point lighthouse is the photograph.

name: Western Maryland Scenic Railroad
unique: A steam locomotive climb from Cumberland to Frostburg over the Allegheny divide, through a horseshoe curve and the 914 foot Brush Tunnel.
buzz: The dome car and the open air car are the seats to book; the Frostburg stop is 90 minutes and the return is the same route.

name: C&O Canal Cumberland
unique: Mile zero of the 184 mile canal towpath, where the canal climbs from Cumberland into the Potomac valley through a lock house and a stone aqueduct.
buzz: Cyclists ride the whole towpath in two days; the first ten miles from Cumberland are flat and shaded and the Paw Paw tunnel is the highlight.

name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
unique: A 3,900 acre lake in the Allegheny mountains with a swimming beach, boat rentals and a ski area at one end, ringed by state forest.
buzz: Summer is the lake and winter is Wisp ski area; the state park beach is the cheap way in and the rental houses fill a year ahead.

name: Swallow Falls State Park
unique: A gorge walk past Muddy Creek Falls, the tallest in the state, under hemlocks that are among the oldest east of the Mississippi.
buzz: The loop is a mile and the falls are the reward; the hemlock canopy keeps it cool in summer and icy in winter.

name: Historic St. Mary's City
unique: The site of Maryland's first capital, with a reconstructed 17th century inn, a tobacco plantation and an ongoing dig that has found the original statehouse.
buzz: The archaeology is the story and the guides are often students; the living history and the ship reconstruction make it a full half day.

name: Point Lookout State Park
unique: A point where the Potomac meets the Chesapeake, with a Civil War prison camp cemetery, a lighthouse and a beach on the bay.
buzz: The prison history is grim and the markers are quiet; the fishing pier and campground are why locals come back.

name: Smith Island
unique: A marshy island of watermen's villages reachable only by boat, where the layer cake is a local invention and golf carts are the main transport.
buzz: The cake is the reason many come and the island is quiet and flat; the ferry takes 45 minutes and the last boat back is early.
